subject: Offline SSD delivery & jump-host acceptance procedure
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Delta Logistics <ops@deltalogistics.com>, AOI Labs Procurement <procurement@aoilabs.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Offline SSD delivery & jump-host acceptance procedure

Team / Delta Ops —

Per AOI Labs' private deployment window (DL-4521), we need to confirm the offline SSD courier and acceptance choreography. Summary of asks below — please confirm ETA and which attachments you will provide to the site operator on delivery.

Key constraints:
- The SSDs will be LUKS-encrypted; manifest and signature will accompany the drive (manifest filename: ssd_package_manifest.json; detached signature: ssd_package_manifest.sig).
- Site will only accept packages if the signature verifies against the public key with fingerprint: 9C:4A:1F:88:2B:6D:AA:11:3F:EA:07:44:99:3B:21:5C.
- Delivery requires two-person custody and operator witness; chain_of_custody.pdf must be handed to AOI operator and returned scanned within 1 hour.

Operational checklist (what Redwood expects on-site):
1) Operator receives sealed, tamper-evident case and checks manifest exists.
2) Verify manifest signature (we provide public key and verification steps).
3) Mount into isolated jump host (details below) — no upstream network until acceptance tests pass.
4) Run canary validation (sha256 checks, image metadata, boot smoke tests).
5) If all good, apply ACL: restrict outgoing access to AOI-allowed update servers only for final pull.

Jump host/network notes (initial ask to network/security):
- Jump host IPs: 10.201.78.11 (primary), 10.201.78.12 (backup) — these are in AOI's management VLAN; firewall should only allow TCP 22 from operator workstation VLAN and TCP 443 to the signed-update endpoint after canary pass.
- We prefer port 10250 closed; no ephemeral outbound allowed during validation window.

Attachments included: canary-runbook.md (stub), verification checklist template.

Please confirm: courier ETA, which document set (digital + hardcopy) you'll hand to the operator, and confirm you can enforce two-person custody.

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Product Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Delta Logistics <ops@deltalogistics.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, AOI Labs Procurement <procurement@aoilabs.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Offline SSD delivery & jump-host acceptance procedure

Priyom / Kimberly —

Confirmed. Courier ETA for site (AOI East DC) is 2026-10-11 09:30 local. Documents we will hand to the operator:
- chain_of_custody.pdf (original, wet-signed)
- ssd_package_manifest.json (printed) + ssd_package_manifest.sig (USB-stick + printed QR)
- manifest verification quicksheet (operator copy)

We will provide two-person custody by default — driver + field supervisor. Photos of tamper seals will be taken at handoff and uploaded to our portal.

Attached to this message (see portal link) are scanned pre-shipment photos and a copy of the manifest signature file. Filename: ssd_package_manifest.sig.

Let us know if you need a local phone contact for the receiving operator — we can supply cell number on request (we do not publish it in email for privacy).

— Delta Ops
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Delta Logistics <ops@deltalogistics.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Offline SSD delivery & jump-host acceptance procedure

Thanks Delta — this layout looks good. A few network specifics AOI's infra team asked to confirm before delivery:

- VLAN / routing: The management VLAN (10.201.78.0/24) will be isolated at the edge ACL until final sign-off. The operator workstation (10.201.120.0/24) will be the only source allowed to SSH into the jump host during validation.
- Firewall rules (pre-acceptance):
  * Ingress: allow TCP 22 from 10.201.120.0/24 -> 10.201.78.11/12; ICMP limited to echo-reply only from operator subnet.
  * Egress: block all outbound except DNS (UDP 53) to AOI internal resolver and NTP (UDP 123) to AOI NTP pool.
  * Post-acceptance temporary rule: allow HTTPS (443) to signed-update.redwood.ai (IP: 34.217.110.45) for a 2-hour window to allow final pull.
- Jump host disk mounts: ensure no auto-mount of external devices; manual attach only.

We will push a jump_host_acl.patch (attached) to AOI's firewall team. Also requesting that Delta confirm the chain_of_custody signer name and title on arrival to match procurement record (AOI contact: Rana Singh).

Kimberly Park
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Delta Logistics <ops@deltalogistics.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, AOI Labs Procurement <procurement@aoilabs.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 07:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Offline SSD delivery & jump-host acceptance procedure

All — thanks for the confirmation. Draft canary plan below (short):

Canary validation steps (30–45m expected):
1) Operator verifies tamper seal and prints manifest.
2) On jump host, operator runs: gpg --verify ssd_package_manifest.sig ssd_package_manifest.json (we will provide GPG public key and fingerprint).
3) Run automated checks: canary-runbook.md -> checksums, image metadata match, boot to single-user console (no network).
4) Record logs to local USB (for audit) and upload the signed log to our secure portal once connectivity window opens.
5) On success, security lead (Jonas) authorizes the 2-hour HTTPS window for final pull. If any step fails, package is sealed and returned to courier — escalation to procurement and security required.

I've attached a short runbook (canary-runbook.md) and a one-line acceptance script (acceptance-stub.sh) for operators.

Please confirm:
- Jonas, can you review and provide explicit authorization criteria?
- Delta, can you confirm you will keep courier on-site for up to 3 hours in case of rework?

Thanks,
Priyom
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Delta Logistics <ops@deltalogistics.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Offline SSD delivery & jump-host acceptance procedure

Good — reviewed. Authorization criteria (short):
- Manifest signature must verify with fingerprint 9C:4A:1F:88:2B:6D:AA:11:3F:EA:07:44:99:3B:21:5C.
- Checksums (sha256) must match manifest entries.
- Boot smoke must reach single-user prompt and show no unexpected kernel modules.
- Chain_of_custody.pdf must be wet-signed on receipt.

If all four are green, I will send a signed approval email (from my account) to AOI operator to open the HTTPS window. If any fail, do not open any external connectivity and return package. Also require that an on-site AOI manager (Rana Singh) be present as witness for final acceptance.

I will stand by my phone during the acceptance window — call me at the number on my signature if anything abnormal occurs.

Jonas Weber
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
From: Delta Logistics <ops@deltalogistics.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, AOI Labs Procurement <procurement@aoilabs.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Offline SSD delivery & jump-host acceptance procedure

Priyom / team —

Status update: delivery completed at 2026-10-11 09:35 local. Operator confirmed receipt, chain_of_custody.pdf wet-signed by Rana Singh. Photographs and tamper-seal logs uploaded to our portal (see link). ssd_package_manifest.sig attached to the parcel and on the courier USB.

We waited on-site for the 2-hour contingency window; AOI completed canary tests and authorized final pull. Please confirm you've received the signed acceptance logs on the portal or want Delta to email copies to your security inbox.

— Delta Logistics
